column2: On the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “If you were to rely on Allah as He truly deserves to be relied upon, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out in the morning with empty stomachs and return in the evening with full stomachs.” Reported by Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Ḥākim; al-Tirmidhī said: Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
“As He truly deserves to be relied upon”: by depending on Allah in all matters.
Taghdū (“they go out in the morning”): they set off at the start of the day,
khimāṣan (“with empty stomachs”): lean-bellied from hunger.
Tarūḥu (“return in the evening”): come back at the end of the day,
biṭānan (“with full stomachs”): with filled bellies.
The virtue of reliance on Allah, and that it is among the greatest means by which provision is brought.
Reliance does not contradict using means, for he described the birds as using the means of provision by going out in the morning and returning in the evening.
A person should use the means of provision and rely on Allah, without being greedy, for provision is decreed and he has done what is required to obtain it.
A servant's faith is not complete without relying on Allah in all his affairs.
This hadith guides us to rely on Allah the Exalted in all our affairs.

The reality of reliance is depending on Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in bringing about benefits and warding off harms in matters of this world and the religion, for none but He, Glorified and Exalted is He, gives, withholds, harms or benefits.

And a person should do the things that bring him benefits and ward off harms from him while relying on Allah: “And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him” [al-Ṭalāq 65:3]; “and upon Him let those who rely [indeed] rely” [Yūsuf 12:67].
Among what has been said on this:
Rely on the Most Merciful in every need / you have, for Allah decrees and ordains.
A man may perish where he feels secure, / and be saved, by Allah's leave, from where he takes precautions.
Another poet:
Rely on the Most Merciful in every matter, / for truly no one who relied on Him has failed.
Be confident in Allah and patient with His decree, / and you will win what you hope for from Him as a favour.
Another poet:
In every situation there is none but Allah, / so let us never rely on anything but His kindness.
How many a situation comes that a young man dislikes, / while the good for him lies in it, against his own wishes!
